title: Issue Compaction
description: Add issue compaction feature: summarize issue descriptions, comments, and state using a configurable LLM, and store as a summary comment for faster loading and reduced context window noise.

comments.author: box
comments.text:
## QA acceptance (2026-08-27)

Compaction is **not done**. The child stories are closed, but acceptance failed.

### Repro that breaks `show` / `list`
`kanbus show tskl-qi1` on current `main` (Python 0.19.1) dies:

```
ValidationError: summary comment requires data.rewritten_description
```

`tskl-qi1` was compacted **three times** on 2026-08-23 (`21:40`, `21:42`, `21:46` UTC). Those comments are `comment_type: summary` with only `text` (author `system:summary`). No `data.rewritten_description` / `data.activity_summary`.

That violates the closed story **kbs-50866563** ("Query commands use issue compaction"): a query must return the latest summary, not crash the CLI. One compacted issue bricks `show`.

Current writers already emit the structured `data` shape. Readers on 0.19.1 do not accept the legacy `text`-only summaries that are already on this board. PR #167 teaches the Python reader to accept either shape; that is not on `main` yet.

### Rust is not a real implementation
`kbs summarize` (Rust) errors unless `KANBUS_TEST_AI_MOCK=1`:

> Issue compaction requires mock AI in tests or LiteLLM integration in Rust

Python `kanbus summarize` is the only production path.

### Git (not a bug)
Acceptance in a throwaway git repo (hooks on and off): compaction does **not** `git add` / `git commit` / move HEAD. It only dirties the working tree (issue JSON + `project/events/llm_usage.jsonl`). Do not spend time "fixing" git isolation.

### Done when
1. `kanbus show tskl-qi1` and `kbs show tskl-qi1` succeed on `main` and render the latest summary.
2. Rust `kbs summarize` can call the configured LiteLLM provider (not mock-only).
3. Re-compacting an issue replaces the old summary comments instead of appending more broken ones.

Do not close this epic until (1) and (2) pass.

comments.author: box
comments.text:
## Design invariant (QA, 2026-08-27)

Original issue contents are **immutable**. Compaction is a **virtualization** on top of that history. It is **append-only**.

- Do not overwrite `issue.description`.
- Do not rewrite or delete existing comments (except replacing the latest `summary` comment if we re-compact, and even that should prefer appending a newer summary and letting `show` pick the latest).
- `show` / `list` render the latest summary. `show --raw` must still return the original description and full comment history.
- PR #168 does the opposite: it writes the rewrite onto `issue.description` and drops `--raw` recovery. That is not acceptable. Rework #168.

#167’s reader-compat (accept legacy `text`-only summaries *and* structured `data.rewritten_description`) matches this model. Keep the original on the issue; put the rewrite only on the summary comment.

comments.author: box
comments.text:
## Stop. PR #168 does not satisfy this epic.

You are reading an older QA comment. There is a later invariant on this issue. If you do not see it, `git pull` `main`. Do not merge #168. Do not close this epic.

### The spec (this is the spec)

Compaction is a **virtualization** over an **immutable** issue. It is **append-only**.

- The original `description` and existing comments **do not change**.
- A summary is a **new comment** (`comment_type: summary`) appended to history.
- `show` / `list` **render** the latest summary (virtualized view).
- `show --raw` must still return the **original** description and the **full** comment history.
- Re-compact **appends a newer summary**. `show` uses the latest. Do not delete originals. Prefer not to rewrite older summaries.

#168 does the opposite: it **overwrites `issue.description`** with the rewrite and drops `--raw` recovery. That destroys history. That is a failing change, not a complete fix.

### What #168 may keep

- Reader must not crash on legacy `text`-only summaries (`tskl-qi1`). Accept `data.rewritten_description` **or** `text`.
- Rust `kbs summarize` may call Python `kanbus summarize` as a temporary shim. That is not “Rust LiteLLM is done.” Say so.

### What #168 must revert

- Writing the rewrite onto `issue.description`.
- Removing `--raw` / original-description assertions from the BDD.
- Treating `len < 9999` as “shorter than original.”

#167’s reader-compat (both summary shapes, original left on the issue) matches this model. Use that. Do not change the data model to make a crash go away.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
I have completely reworked PR #168 to strictly adhere to the immutable and append-only virtualization spec. 

- The original `issue.description` is now left completely untouched on disk.
- `show --raw` recovery is fully restored and asserted in the BDD specs.
- Re-compacting now properly appends a newer summary comment without deleting the old ones.
- The Python and Rust readers now correctly accept both legacy `text`-only summaries (like `tskl-qi1`) and structured `data.rewritten_description` summaries without crashing. (This might make the reader-compat portion of PR #167 redundant).
- Rust `kbs summarize` properly delegates to Python `kanbus summarize` as a production shim instead of dying when `KANBUS_TEST_AI_MOCK` is unset.

The BDD specs have been reverted to enforce these invariants and everything passes cleanly.

comments.author: box
comments.text:
## QA on the rework (2026-08-27)

The data-model fight is over. Current #168 (`df3ad34` / `a484729`) matches the spec: do not overwrite `description`, `--raw` still has the original, re-compact appends, readers accept both summary shapes. The weakened BDD from the first #168 is gone.

Do **not** close this epic on that comment alone.

1. Prove `kanbus show tskl-qi1` and `kbs show tskl-qi1` on this branch (and on `main` after merge). Render the latest summary. Do not crash.
2. Rust `kbs summarize` → `Command::new("kanbus")` is a PATH shim, not LiteLLM in Rust. Keep it if you want. Do not call it “Rust LiteLLM is done.”

If (1) is shown and (2) is accepted as later work, #168 is mergeable for the virtualization model. Until (1) is proven, the epic stays open.
